messages.content: Write the charter for a newly formed platform engineering team. Around 250 words.

# Platform Engineering — Team Charter

## Purpose

We build and run the internal platform that product teams deploy on. Our measure of success is their throughput, not ours: a team that has never met us should be able to ship a service to production on their first week, and know where to look when it breaks.

## Scope

We own the paved road — CI/CD pipelines, environment provisioning, service scaffolding, observability defaults, and the runtime substrate underneath them. We do not own product code, and we do not gatekeep it. Teams that need to leave the paved road may, provided they take on the operational load they inherit by doing so.

## How we work

Treat the platform as a product and its users as customers who can walk away. That means published interfaces, real documentation, deprecation notices with dates attached, and a support channel someone actually watches. Golden paths are opinionated and optional; mandates are a last resort and require a written reason.

We prefer boring technology, small reversible changes, and defaults that are safe when nobody is paying attention.

## Commitments

- Publish and defend SLOs for every service we operate.
- Respond to platform incidents ahead of feature work, always.
- Run a monthly review with two product teams to hear what the platform costs them.
- Say no in writing, with reasoning, rather than by silence.

## First six months

Consolidate the three existing deploy pipelines into one, establish a service catalog, and cut median time-to-first-deploy for a new service to under a day. We will report progress against those three numbers.

output:
# Platform Engineering — Team Charter

## Purpose

We build and operate the internal platform other teams deploy on. Our success shows up in their numbers, not ours: someone who has never spoken to us should get a service into production in their first week, and know where to look the night it falls over.

## Scope

Ours: build pipelines, environment provisioning, service templates, observability defaults, and the runtime underneath all of it. Not ours: product code. We are not a review board for it, either. Any team may go its own way, so long as it carries the operational weight that choice creates.

## How we work

The platform is a product, and its users can leave. So: documented interfaces, documentation that matches the code, deprecations announced with a date attached, and a support channel with a human reading it. The default path is opinionated and optional. When we require something, we write down why.

We favor dull technology, changes small enough to undo, and defaults that hold up when nobody is watching.

## Commitments

- Publish SLOs for everything we operate, and defend them.
- Platform incidents come before feature work. No exceptions.
- Sit down monthly with two product teams and hear what we cost them.
- When the answer is no, say no in writing, with a reason. Never by silence.

## First six months

Fold three deploy pipelines into one. Stand up a service catalog. Get median time-to-first-deploy for a new service under a day. Those three numbers are what we report on.
